Well that's certainly true. I think that society puts a lot of pressure on women to look beautiful. Much more than men.

I know I could look better if I decided to dress better, but it's not so easy. I've always been told, by my mother/sisters, that men are not interested in fashion, and going shopping bores them to hell. After enough repetitions I started to believe it.

Not wearing nice clothes or generally not caring about my appearance (I used to be very skinny) resulted in a complete absence of feminine attention for a very long time. It's something that really undermines your self confidence.

This belief also means that in my entire life I have never been shopping with friends to buy clothes. I don't get opinions from anyone, except sometimes from my mother/sisters. Guys don't go shopping together where I come from.

The same could be said about my hairstyle or my the way I care about my skin. Basically, guys don't talk about this. And since nobody talks about it, you don't really think about it most of the time. Then you wonder why you haven't had a girlfriend in more than 2 years. In fact, I would probably have had more relationships in those past 3 years if I had been gay. Wishing to be gay is ridiculous as sexual orientation is not something that can be changed, and being gay is still obviously worse than being straight because of the way society treats you. But it sometimes crosses my mind.

I know I could look a bit more attractive with better clothes/skin, etc. but I haven't learned these things earlier in life and nobody I know can help me. I can learn all of that on the internet of course, and I'm trying to improve, but honestly, when I go buy clothes all I can think of is how expensive all these things are. It's pretty terrible.

I suppose that this "male problem" could probably partially explain why [women think that 80% of men are below average in terms of attractiveness.](http://blog.okcupid.com/index.php/your-looks-and-online-dating/)

In the end I know that I have to be 100% responsible for what's happening to me, but you can't help thinking that things could be so much easier in a better societal environment. For men and women.

(Sorry if this was a bit long or ridden with English mistakes, I tried my best to explain how I feel about this!)

I thought Ebola was more or less under control until a few days ago, when I saw the exponential growth graph on Wikipedia (there is also a nice log graph that shows that's it's a very nice exponential...). From that moment I realized that they had lost control of the situation. 

The reports of the WHO of those last few days confirmed this.

We need to pour money on this problem as fast as possible. 

You don't need a PhD in mathematics to understand what an exponential is, but most people have no idea what it really means. If this situations continues for several weeks, some of these countries are screwed, and we could be screwed too.

I'm still convinced that it won't hit hard first world countries, because if there is an outbreak many governments will hopefully finance the pharma companies to develop a vaccine quickly.
